name: Queer anarchism
summary: Queer anarchism holds that queer liberation requires ending the state, capitalism, patriarchy, heteronormativity and the gender binary through social revolution and direct action. It rejects the mainstream gay-rights agenda of marriage, military inclusion and hate-crime law as assimilation, and favours autonomous queer communities, relationship autonomy and prison and police abolition.
scope: The contemporary anarchist current of the 2000s onward as presented in the anthology Queering Anarchism (Daring, Rogue, Shannon, Volcano, 2012) and summarised on Wikipedia, with Emma Goldman as a historical precursor on marriage and free love. Excludes liberal LGBT rights movements and non-anarchist queer theory. Many statements are not addressed by these sources, so a large share of answers are low-confidence inferences from anti-statism and anti-capitalism.

sources.title: Queering Anarchism
sources.author: C.B. Daring, J. Rogue, Deric Shannon, Abbey Volcano (eds.)
sources.usedFor: Introduction and early chapters on state, property, marriage, gender, sex work, hate crime laws and assimilation.

sources.title: Marriage and Love
sources.author: Emma Goldman
sources.usedFor: Anarchist critique of marriage, Church and State, and free love and motherhood.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Queer anarchists want care free of state gatekeeping and criticise tying health care to marital status; they would favour universal access but through mutual aid rather than the state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage reform is a reformist state measure that anarchists treat as secondary to abolishing wage labour; adherents split between supporting gains and rejecting the framing.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Anarchism opposes capitalism and the intro condemns rent and wage exploitation; markets are not seen as a liberator.

public-ownership.rationale: Anarchists reject state ownership as another form of political power; they favour common or collective ownership instead.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses taxation; anarchists want to abolish the wealth hierarchy and the state that taxes, so the reformist measure is neither endorsed nor central.

unions-good.rationale: Class struggle is held central to queer organising, which implies support for worker self-organisation, though sources do not discuss unions specifically.

property-fundamental.rationale: The introduction defines property as claims on things one neither uses nor occupies and treats it as a source of exploitation.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Adherents want to abolish capitalism and the state, not manage corporations through state regulation; inferred from their anti-state stance.

cut-welfare.rationale: They criticise state systems yet object to cuts that harm queer and poor people; inferred, with support for mutual aid in place of the state.

worker-ownership.rationale: Anti-capitalist class analysis favours workers' self-management and common control of production, in line with anarchism generally.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Queer anarchists oppose state coercion and policing, and queer communities have been targets of surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Anti-authoritarian bodily autonomy implies support, though the sources do not discuss drugs; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The introduction lists hate crime legislation among mainstream gay-rights goals that queer anarchists criticise, as it expands the state's penal power.

strong-leader.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy and rulers entirely.

state-harmful.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state as a system of rule, and argue it enforces rigid gender and sexual categories.

limit-guns.rationale: Anarchists generally distrust state disarmament and queer anarchist anthologies defend armed self-defence; inferred and contested.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and prisons are described as instruments of state coercion; abolition is a goal.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: C.B. Daring argues anarchists should treat sex work without the moralism common in radical critiques; decriminalisation follows.

decide-locally.rationale: Self-determination and building society from the ground up favour local autonomy, though they go further than local government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Adherents seek prison abolition, so they reject framing prisons as the answer even if rehabilitative.

traditional-family.rationale: Anarchism and queer theory both reject structures built on the nuclear family and capitalism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Contributors criticise gay marriage campaigns as reinforcing the state and nuclear family, yet most would not oppose legal access; split between opposing the institution and defending individuals' rights. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Goldman backed free motherhood chosen rather than compelled, and bodily autonomy is central to queer anarchism.

more-religion-public.rationale: Anarchists oppose Church as well as State, as Goldman does in her marriage critique.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anti-oppression politics implies agreement, but anarchists prefer direct action over state remedies; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Transfeminism as presented by J. Rogue treats gender as socially constructed and rejects biological essentialism.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nationalism is rejected; Conrad calls for freedom of movement across nation-state borders.

gradual-change.rationale: Queer anarchists favour direct action and social revolution over gradualism within existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Border enforcement is criticised and free movement is advocated.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: They oppose state power at every level and so distrust the UN; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Opposition to capitalism and pink capitalism; Seattle 1999 WTO protests involved queer anarchists.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Anarchists oppose state militaries, though some accept human rights aims; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Conrad's call for freedom of movement across nation-state borders reflects the standard anarchist position.

limit-growth.rationale: Sources do not address ecology; adherents are split between eco-anarchists and others.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Concern for climate is common but drastic government action conflicts with anti-statism; split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; anti-capitalist scepticism of technocratic solutions inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; anarchist distrust of centralised state-run power inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The sources present social revolution as the path to queer liberation.

experts-over-public.rationale: Anti-hierarchy politics rejects rule by experts.

central-planning.rationale: State planning is a concentration of political power that anarchists reject.

socialized-markets.rationale: They prefer non-market common provision, though worker-owned markets are tolerated by some strands; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: A state tax scheme is not their route; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Anti-property but state taxation is not their method; split.

basic-income.rationale: Some like unconditional support, others reject dependence on the state; contested.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist economic protection conflicts with anti-nation, anti-capitalist stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of the economy is rejected.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property as claims over unused things is rejected, though small possession is tolerated.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The introduction describes exploitation through rent and wages and aims at ending the system.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anarchists oppose central banks but not in order to leave money to the market; split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies are hierarchical and statist.

one-party-rule.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and political hierarchy outright, so rule by one party is opposed; the sources do not discuss party states as such.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule is a form of the political hierarchy anarchists oppose; the sources do not take up monarchy specifically.

democracy-best.rationale: They favour direct self-organisation over representative states, which are criticised as systems of rule and representation.

direct-votes.rationale: Prefer consensus and direct participation, but not state voting on laws; split.

workers-councils.rationale: Self-managed councils fit anarchism, but they do not claim 'political power' in the statement's sense; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Self-determination is endorsed, with anarchists favouring dissolution of state power.

natural-rulers.rationale: Queering Anarchism argues for a highly egalitarian ethos and against all hierarchy, which rules out a natural ruling class, though the claim is not addressed directly. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: The editors describe a destructive impulse against systems of domination, quoting Bakunin, and the BashBack anthology advocates militancy.

war-builds-character.rationale: Opposed to militarism and state wars.

separate-church-state.rationale: Opposition to both Church and State; they go beyond separation to abolish the state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Goldman treats Church and State as joint instruments of control.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Policing and courts are tools of coercion; anarcho-capitalist privatisation is not their view.

military-superiority.rationale: Queering Anarchism praises gay liberationists for rejecting militarism and lists the military among the institutions that maintain hegemony, so national military dominance is opposed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Opposed to nationalism and in favour of free movement.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Gayge Operaista argues class struggle should be central to queer organising; its place in all of history is not claimed.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Anti-capitalist egalitarianism favours material equality; inferred.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Recent queer anarchist work engages anti-colonial politics; inferred from decolonial leanings.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; anti-colonial but suspicious of state-to-state payments.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nation and bloc building is rejected.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Many draw on Stirner's egoism but mutual aid is also central; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The sources say nothing about ecology; adherents include eco-anarchists but the profile has no stated view, so it stays neutral.

limit-population.rationale: Coercive population control is opposed; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Anarcho-primitivism exists but is not mainstream; split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Includes the Gender Accelerationist Manifesto but not typical of mainstream; split.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily self-determination, including transition, is central.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Government in any form is rejected.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Resistance to surveillance implies support; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Queer anarchists seek to overturn inherited norms of gender, family and sexuality rather than restore them; the sources do not address a lost social order as such.

direct-action.rationale: Queer anarchists use direct action, squats and autonomous zones.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative communities and building from the ground up reflect this.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Anti-hierarchy ideas imply it but it is not stressed.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Anarchist communism supplies this; the sources stress anti-capitalism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The introduction describes exploitation through rent and wages.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The book's introduction frames anarchism as a struggle against the state itself, proposing autonomy, solidarity and mutual aid in its place, which excludes any transitional workers' state.

collective-farming.rationale: Agriculture is not discussed; anarchist traditions include both collectivist and individual smallholder models, so adherents are split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anarchists reject the state but reject the right-libertarian property view behind this claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Anti-state, so they reject state restriction, but wrongful harm is not claimed as the only limit; split. The cited sources do not address this directly, so the answer is inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Collective liberation is emphasised alongside the individual; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Opposition to militarism and state coercion implies rejecting conscription, which the sources do not discuss.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The sources do not weigh leaving against voting; they reject the state as a whole, so neither is privileged.

state-as-business.rationale: Reject the state and market logic.

positive-liberty.rationale: Self-determination plus material means follows from anti-capitalism.

media-academia-power.rationale: No source compares the power of media and universities with elected officials; queer anarchists locate power in state and capital instead.

total-state.rationale: Anarchists oppose the state outright, and the sources describe it as enforcing rigid gender and sexual categories, so a state directing all life is the opposite of their aim.

national-rebirth.rationale: A nationalist project of rebirth is foreign to an anti-state, anti-border politics; the sources do not discuss national decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: An essay in Queering Anarchism calls borders between nations fictions, so expanding a nation's territory runs against the book's politics, though expansion is not discussed.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule through personal oaths to a lord is a hierarchy anarchists oppose; feudal authority is not discussed in the sources.

bound-labor.rationale: Binding peasants to a lord is coerced labour, which the anarchist commitment to autonomy and anticapitalism rejects; the sources do not discuss serfdom.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Queer theory's questioning of the normal and the 'queer' as verb making ideas strange.

universal-morality.rationale: Rejects normative thinking in favour of unfixed practice.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship by return is a nation-state matter the sources do not address; they favour free movement for all, but reject citizenship privileges.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Supports workers' self-management though aims beyond votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market logic is rejected but state schooling is too; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed; anarchists treat state budgets as secondary to abolishing the state and capitalism.

economic-freedom.rationale: They reject capitalism, which the introduction links to exploitation through rent and wages, so they do not hold that political freedom rests on market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Prefigurative example matters but rulers are rejected; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: They reject states and nationalism; self-determination is individual and communal.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Not addressed; desire and pleasure are stressed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The book calls categories of citizenship and borders between nations fictions, and criticises state benefits that reach only people with citizenship status, so limiting welfare to citizens is opposed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Opposes coercive wage labour and state conditionality.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; queer anarchists reject normative tradition but no source calls for destroying libraries or museums.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-imperialist in spirit but opposed to states forming blocs; no source addresses this, so adherents are neutral.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The book criticises marriage for reinforcing prescribed gender roles and patriarchy and argues against the gender binary itself, so laws fixing separate roles for men and women are rejected.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; they oppose exploitation through rent and wages but do not discuss legal bans on lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Legal racial classification is a state enforcement of categories, which queer anarchists oppose as they oppose enforced gender and sexual categories.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The war on capitalism must be a war on all institutions of political power; the state is more than a class tool.

elite-replacement.rationale: A racial replacement conspiracy runs against the book's commitment to dismantling white supremacy; it is not discussed directly.

proportional-representation.rationale: They reject representation but would prefer fairer to less fair; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: The book describes how Europe, through colonisation and imperialism, violently exported its ideas including the gender binary, which it treats as a harm rather than a mission.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anarchism aims at ending patriarchy, heteronormativity and the gender binary.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Opposed to rulers as a system.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Its chapter on queerness and disability names the threat of eugenic extermination as common ground between queer and disability activism and criticises the eugenicist roots of the 'norm'.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Police are seen as coercive tools; accountability is not their main frame.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Anarchists reject the state even in a minimal form, and the sources treat police and prisons as coercive tools that should be abolished.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The book ties queer liberation to dismantling white supremacy and opposes state and social policing of intimacy, which implies rejecting this; interracial marriage is not discussed directly.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Egalitarian though they criticise equality before state law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The theory of socialism in one country is a Marxist-Leninist debate that the sources never address, so neutral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Opposes both state and Church control.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Opposes state bans on practices; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The introduction sets anarchism against the state as such, calling for a struggle against the state and capitalism together, so a socialist state growing stronger is the opposite of its aim.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rejects authority altogether rather than grounding it in consent.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority is state coercion of the kind anarchists oppose; the sources do not discuss expulsions.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rejects competition as the engine of social life.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anarchist freedom is freedom from domination in all its forms.

separated-powers.rationale: They want to abolish rather than divide power.

vanguard-party.rationale: Queering Anarchism notes that anarchists strongly oppose vanguardism and challenge the elitism of anyone claiming authority to lead.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Specific housing policy is not covered; they condemn rent and property claims but do not take a view on state tenant schemes.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Blames institutions such as property and state. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Queer anarchism celebrates difference and opposes enforced norms, which implies rejecting this; the sources do not address diversity and cohesion directly.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Anarchists oppose state repression in any circumstance, so emergency powers against internal enemies are rejected, though the sources do not discuss them.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose markets yet distrust state controls, and the sources are silent.

party-controls-media.rationale: Control of information by a government or party is a form of state authority anarchists reject; media control is not discussed in the sources.

party-commands-army.rationale: Anarchists oppose both standing armies and parties wielding state power; how armies are commanded is not discussed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Hostility to borders and citizenship categories implies opposing long waits for citizenship; naturalisation rules are not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Anarchists reject heads of state and armies alike, so neither arrangement is endorsed; the sources do not discuss constitutional command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Goldman attacks the Church as an institution of control alongside the State, which implies rejecting episcopal authority, though church governance is not discussed.

clerical-rule.rationale: Following Goldman's critique of Church and State alike, rule by clerics is an authority they reject.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Opposes state wars; revolutionary defeatism is a classic anarchist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Queer anarchists oppose moral policing of desire and expression, which implies rejecting moral censorship of art; censorship itself is not discussed.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They reject presidencies and rulers altogether, so they would not endorse unlimited terms, though term limits are not a concern for them.

recall-officials.rationale: Mandated recallable delegates fit anarchist practice; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Rent is condemned but each-family ownership is not their model.

people-in-arms.rationale: Some militant strands favour armed community defence; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rural queer anarchists exist but no value claim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not addressed; the sources are largely written by academics and activists and make no claim about educated people.

death-penalty.rationale: The book backs prison abolition and treats the penal system as state violence against queer people, which implies opposing executions; the death penalty is not discussed directly.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sexual liberation, though they distrust state schooling.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anti-religious; but state curricula are not defended; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Daring urges analysis of the sex industry without moralism.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Treating citizenship as a fiction implies rejecting rules that pass it by descent; how citizenship is acquired is not discussed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is not discussed; they would value minority cultures but not look to state schooling and elections.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose religious authority but also state coercion, so adherents are neutral on exemptions from general laws.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Queer politics rejects the normal and values making things strange.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Capitalism and state critique implies it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Trading political freedom for development is authoritarian rule anarchists oppose; development policy is not discussed.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Mutual aid yes; state aid unclear.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: They oppose state militaries and nationalism, so a national nuclear arsenal runs against their politics. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not covered by the sources; state action on risk conflicts with anti-statism though concern is common.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose state conquest but also reject the nation-state frame of territorial claims.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Opposes both Church and State powers.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Anarchists want no head of state at all, symbolic or not; the sources do not discuss the office.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Using armed force to hold a state together is state coercion anarchists oppose; secession is not discussed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; they favour autonomy but reject state sovereignty, so the question does not map onto their politics.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred and divine head of state is both hierarchical rule and religious authority, each rejected by anarchists. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

character-from-environment.rationale: Gender and norms are socially constructed.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Opposes rulers, though also rejects law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed in any source consulted; no stated position on space.

leader-cult.rationale: Anarchism rejects rulers and glorification of leaders as expressions of hierarchy. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not covered; they challenge the nuclear family and state courts, so adherents lack a shared view.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate within state socialism that the sources do not cover; neutral.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The book treats categories of nationality and borders as fictions, which implies rejecting territorial claims based on them; such claims are not discussed.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Goldman's critique of Church and State as joint instruments of control implies opposing religious law enforced by the state; apostasy is not discussed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Legally enforced dress codes for women are the kind of policed gender norms queer anarchists reject; the sources do not discuss them.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not addressed; they oppose money, wage labour and states, so neither side is endorsed.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose nationalism and state schools but support communal self-determination, so neutral.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; they reject nation-state homelands, but also citizenship-based rights, so neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Not stated in the sources; they weigh class and economy alongside gender and sexuality, so neutral.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose capitalism yet also state subsidy of firms, so adherents have no consistent view.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; they reject both state courts and majority rule over minorities, so neutral.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose free trade and state regulation alike, so no clear stance.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; they want a society beyond wage labour, but the sources do not discuss incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Anthology of militancy exists but not typical.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy and inherited advantage, and the sources attack property claims as a basis for rule.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule over others for their benefit is domination, which anarchists reject, and it is colonial in framing. No cited source discusses this statement directly.

patriotic-education.rationale: The sources reject nationalism and favour free movement, so teaching loyalty to flag and anthem is opposed.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Not addressed; they hold that capitalism must be overthrown but make no stated claim about its crises.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The book treats European colonisation and imperialism as violent, which implies opposing a post-imperial sphere of influence; that policy is not discussed.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; anti-capitalist but internationalist, so delinking is neither endorsed nor rejected.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; neutral.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; they reject state treaties generally, but no source discusses colonial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: They reject rulers and representation, so electing rulers is not their model, though it is better than inheritance.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; anarchist circles often show animal-liberation concern, inferred at low confidence.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between vegan and other positions.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: They organise in autonomous zones and take direct action.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critique of pink capitalism and polished corporate Pride.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not discussed in the sources; neutral.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anarchists reject both state offices and citizenship distinctions, so reserving offices for the native-born is opposed, though it is not discussed.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate among communist parties; anarchists reject parties and the sources do not address it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; mutual aid is valued but state development policy is outside the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Treating national borders as fictions implies rejecting claims to recover lost territory; the sources do not discuss irredentism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; they reject ruling hierarchies of any group, though anti-colonial sympathies exist.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists criticise both fascism and Soviet statism but sources take no position on equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Opposition to racial oppression leads adherents to reject this claim; inferred from anti-racism rather than stated in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose national symbols and commemoration of rulers, inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; they critique patriarchy and the gender binary, and the sources take no stance on programmes for boys and men.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed; adherents critique state responses to violence, and the sources take no position on symmetry.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; they reject state institutions everywhere, so the framing does not fit.

military-guardian-role.rationale: They oppose militaries and political rule by armed forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wages are rejected but care is valued; split.

office-by-exam.rationale: They reject government office; exams are less objectionable than election but remain a ruling hierarchy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Goldman rejects marriage as controlling; free ending follows.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property as claims on unused things is rejected.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents recognise structural oppression but distrust state anti-discrimination law.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Critique of pink capitalism and homonormative consumerism.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: They oppose state militaries and foreign policy; state-sponsored armed proxies are a form of state power.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Military intervention by a great power is state violence and domination anarchists oppose; alliance politics are not discussed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-capitalist, with direct action against pink capitalism.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; they reject both states and the premise that democracies are peaceful, so no stance.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's authority to command.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Queer anarchists reject the absolutist non-aggression view and defend militant resistance to domination, as in the BashBack anthology and Bakunin's creative destruction.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: A closed national or imperial bloc contradicts their anti-nationalist, anti-border position and free movement.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State blocking of purchases is a nationalist measure they reject, though they also oppose corporate takeovers; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Conrad argues marriage is tied to property transfers and state benefits and that health care should not depend on marital status.

non-intervention.rationale: Anti-statist anarchists oppose state military intervention, though solidarity with oppressed queer people abroad cuts against an absolute rule; inferred from anti-statism.

industrial-unions.rationale: The sources do not address union structure; queer anarchists favour autonomous, non-hierarchical organising over any single union model, so this is left neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The tradition centres solidarity with persecuted minorities and opposes scapegoating, so it rejects conspiracy claims against a minority.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state secrecy and surveillance; anarchists would favour open information though they do not seek legal rights from the state.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and mutual-aid, self-organised communities, which favour local production over global capital; the sources do not address it directly.

informal-organisation.rationale: Queer anarchism favours autonomous, non-hierarchical groups and direct action; inferred from this, as the sources do not set out a rule against permanent federations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and its constitutions, so they would not rank national law above international law; inferred from anti-nationalism and anti-statism.

religious-nation.rationale: Queer anarchism rejects the nation-state, organised religion and heteronormative moral orders, so a religiously defined nation is opposed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anarchism rejects hierarchy among states and peoples alike, so ritual submission and tribute would be refused; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Anarchists favour mutual aid across communities rather than territorial revenue hoarding; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Anarchists commonly distinguish personal property from the productive property they want held in common; the cited texts discuss property critically, so this is inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anarchists oppose Leninist communism but not through state campaigns; disagreement with 'defeating' it is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Anarchists want services run by communities, not a state-funded mix with private providers; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Goldman attacks the Church as a pillar of oppression alongside the State, which supports mild agreement, but the illusion thesis is inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anti-capitalism is core to the current, so a progressive role for capitalism would be rejected; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The current holds that patriarchy and capitalism are intertwined and must be ended together.

socialized-care.rationale: Adherents want collective care but are split between mutual aid and public provision, since public means state; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Anti-nationalist and anti-assimilationist; purging foreign words would be rejected, inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Anarchists reject state treaties yet support indigenous sovereignty; adherents would split, inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Autonomous queer communities and mutual aid are favoured, though not necessarily small property-holding ones; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and anti-nationalism, which oppose state-directed ethnic settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Anarchism rejects both state capitalism and state communism in favour of a stateless alternative; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anti-statist and anti-nationalist, queer anarchists distrust territorial claims; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; an adherent rejects it from a commitment to anti-oppression solidarity.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The current opposes state regulation of sex and criticises the criminalisation of queer lives.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Anarchism is hostile to state repression and favours autonomous community organisation.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Anarchists reject Church and State both, as Goldman's critique argues, and oppose any state punishment of belief.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Queer anarchists reject the state and capitalism, and so colonial rule for a ruling country's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; adherents likely split between anti-imperialist solidarity and distrust of religious politics.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Anarchists reject religious and state authority and oppose rule by force; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct action, autonomous communities and rejecting hierarchy make direct participation central.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Queering Anarchism treats race, gender, sexuality and class as interlocking systems of domination.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The current rejects the gender binary and supports trans people, though some distrust state legal recognition; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Relationship and bodily autonomy lead adherents to favour it, though they would prefer mutual aid over state regulation; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Anarchists place themselves outside the left-right state spectrum yet reject mixing with right ideas; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: The anthology criticises capitalism and wage labour as alienating, a standard anarchist critique.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Solidarity against oppression makes adherents reject such claims; not addressed in the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Anarchism rejects all authority, divine or governmental, and Goldman attacks the Church's claims.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Anti-state; adherents would oppose bans on dress but also state religion, so views are split; inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Adherents oppose silencing victims of harassment, though they distrust courts; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Queer anarchists reject both capitalism and the state, so a regulated market economy is rejected.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-statism and police and prison abolition lead adherents to reject standing armies; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: Anticapitalist anarchists reject the notion that elites should grow rich first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Opposition to the state and war leads adherents to reject great-power blocs; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Queer anarchism rejects the state and all hierarchy, so inherited office is opposed.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Anarchists split between mutualist banking and abolishing credit and money; the sources do not address it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalism and anti-statism, which oppose creditor-imposed policy; the sources do not discuss austerity.

property-franchise.rationale: It rejects the state and capitalist hierarchy, so a vote tied to wealth is opposed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to patriarchy and to all domination; the sources link these generally, not women and nature specifically.

reification.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalism, which broadly follows the anarchist critique of markets; the term is not used in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from its anti-capitalism; formal freedoms are seen as limited by class power, though the sources do not address media ownership.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of the state and its courts; anarchists oppose state law and decree alike.

racial-franchise.rationale: It opposes all hierarchy and domination, including racial, and rejects state citizenship as the basis for rights.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic for the sources; adherents favour direct participation but are wary of online platforms.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists favour transparency but reject state records as a framework.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of state control over marriage and relationships; the objection is to legal marriage itself.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to bigotry and hierarchy; the sources do not address boycotts.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Anarchists favour direct democracy and horizontal decision-making, which fits deliberation by ordinary people, but they reject state institutions that would convene and empower an assembly; inferred from these principles.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Queer anarchists reject inherited authority and would favour believers rethinking doctrine in light of queer experience, though many are simply anti-religious; inferred from anti-authoritarian and anti-heteronormative principles.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Queer anarchists target capitalism and property as sources of domination, so concentrated wealth is read as a threat to freedom, though they frame it as class power rather than a liberty-and-law argument.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The introduction describes an anti-assimilationist ethic that rejects military inclusion as a gay-rights priority, since anarchists oppose the military itself.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism: anarchists reject the state running schools or imposing any belief, including unbelief.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Prison and police abolition is part of the movement's stated programme alongside autonomous queer communities.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from rejection of the state and of fixed identity categories; guaranteed communal shares of government entrench group identities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred: anarchists prefer voluntary community mutual aid to state programmes, though they distinguish it from hierarchical charity.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from hostility to political careers and rulers; rotation of delegates fits anarchist practice, though elected office is itself rejected.

vote-delegation.rationale: Revocable delegation resembles anarchist recallable delegates, but anarchists reject voting-based representation; adherents would split.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents focus on present struggles against state and capital, and nothing here settles the question.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from opposition to gender hierarchy, though many adherents reject organised religion and care little about its offices.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Goldman describes marriage as subjecting women to male authority, and the anthology opposes hierarchy in intimate relationships, so spouses should be equals.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and rejection of borders and citizenship hierarchies; adherents oppose excluding residents from political participation.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-capitalism and opposition to housing as commodity, though anarchists prefer squatting and mutual aid to state caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and critique of property; the sources do not discuss patents directly.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Queer anarchism opposes militarism, nationalism and state control, so drilled national-service youth movements are inferred to be strongly rejected.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from anti-militarism and anti-statism; the sources do not discuss nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from anti-militarism and anti-imperialism; the sources do not discuss bases directly.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anarchists distrust state acts, but queer anarchists value remembrance of persecution; the sources do not address recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and the anarchist critique of rent, profit and inherited property.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists split between pacifism and defence, but most queer anarchists endorse direct action and defence of communities against violence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Queer anarchism rejects nationalism and treats national identities as constructed; inferred from anti-statism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Queering Anarchism draws on queer theory, where Butler holds sex is as constructed as gender, and the sources attack the gender binary.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Queer anarchism rejects the gender binary and fixed identity categories, which implies feminist politics should not rest on a fixed 'women'.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Anti-nationalist and anti-statist, so honouring national martyrs as saints is inferred to be strongly rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The movement is secular and materialist, so a good-versus-evil spiritual framing is inferred to be strongly rejected.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from anti-nationalism; the sources do not discuss diaspora and homeland.

culture-before-state.rationale: Anti-nationalist and anti-statist, so national cultural renewal is not a project it would prioritise; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from critique of patriarchy and the gender binary; adherents are mostly secular and critical of religion but accept inclusive language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from critique of patriarchy; adherents are secular and critical of religion but would judge traditions on gender justice.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Anti-nationalist and anti-hierarchical, so privileging a national majority in economic life is inferred to be strongly rejected.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Anti-statist and anti-nationalist, so ethnic territorial units are inferred to be rejected.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism: adherents favour autonomous worker organisation and direct action over state-linked unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: anarchists want workers' self-management, though they would phrase it as abolishing political power rather than holding it.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: adherents want such services run by communities and mutual aid, not by the state, so state hands and public hands pull apart.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: anarchists reject legislatures and representative government altogether.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from anarcho-communist commons and community ownership, though it is not limited to the locality.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: anarchist federalism has delegated, mandated coordination with decisions kept in local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the critique of the nuclear family and heteronormativity; a family-support wage presumes that model.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows, though trans health access might push toward speed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and no principle clearly decides it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and mistrust of surveillance, with no source addressing it.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from queer communities' reliance on pseudonyms and privacy, and from anarchist opposition to state surveillance.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred: adherents reject the state, but they firmly reject treating people as means to community or state ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are mostly secular but not hostile to spirituality as such.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: self-government should rest on its own autonomy, not on powers a national legislature grants.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and distrust of corporate control of agriculture.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; no clear position follows.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Inferred: adherents oppose racism and back autonomous organising by oppressed groups, but reject identity-based interests as a general rule.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: pride for oppressed groups is accepted, while pride for dominant groups is not; the statement is general.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: anarchists reject standing armies and states, so they would not endorse armed forces even for national defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Inferred from anarchist opposition to nations and states; the sources treat identity as fluid and reject state-defined categories.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of state structures and religious authority over intimate life, which the sources apply to marriage and Church and State.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and anti-nationalism; an anarchist would not speak for 'my country' or fear its break-up.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from anti-capitalism and opposition to class barriers, though queer anarchists would prefer free autonomous education to a state one.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from distrust of state and market mechanisms; anarchists favour direct action and communal control over taxation.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the anti-capitalist, ecological outlook common among anarchists; the sources do not address it directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources reject the gender binary and essentialist gender categories, so an adherent would not assign distinct values to women as a group.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from anarchist anti-militarism, though 'national safety' is a state framing they would reject.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Anarchists reject state diplomacy altogether, so the question of open versus secret treaties is not their framing.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from anarchist hostility to state control and to borders; they would also oppose unrestricted capital, so the pull is weak.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Queer anarchists reject the state and its police and military and favour police abolition, so a state arms monopoly is the opposite of their aim.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The anti-assimilationist ethic rejects military service and war as state institutions, so refusing to fight in state wars fits it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed directly; anarchists favour collective workplace organization and direct action, though many prefer worker control to bargaining with employers, inferred from anarchist labour tradition.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; queer anarchists want people to get support through mutual aid rather than state benefits, so a state tax-credit scheme is inferred to be disliked.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; legal borrowing limits are state fiscal machinery, and the anti-capitalist, anti-statist stance suggests no investment in them.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed; anti-capitalism and opposition to imperialism suggest sympathy, but the aim is abolition of states rather than a fairer order among them.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Anarchists seek to abolish the state and build new forms of social organization, not to capture it, which the introduction presents as the core of the anarchism in the anthology.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Anarchists reject a single blueprint and favour autonomous communities, though the sources opened do not state this about the economy.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not addressed; pricing nature extends commodification, which anarchist anti-capitalism opposes.

sacred-nation.rationale: Queer anarchists reject nationalism along with the state, and anti-assimilationism rejects patriotic institutions.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; the anti-capitalist stance suggests sympathy for cancelling debt, though through direct action more than government.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; critique of domination by states and capital extends to core-periphery relations, inferred from anti-statism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The anthology challenges the gender binary and natural categories of sex and identity, so a fixed shared human nature is rejected.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; state-funded media is a state institution, and queer anarchists favour autonomous media, inferred from anti-statism.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed; queer anarchists reject authority and orthodoxy, and inferred from that they would see religions' rival doctrines as hierarchies rather than one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists oppose state intervention but favour farmer mutual aid and cooperative credit, so an adherent could go either way.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from anti-statism and anti-militarism that queer anarchists want no state to hold nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists generally reject electoral parties and the state, so a workers' party in government is inferred to be disagreed with.

ban-fgm.rationale: Adherents would oppose the practice yet distrust criminal law and the state, so they are inferred to be split on a legal ban.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from opposition to patriarchy; they would support equal treatment of women while rejecting state-backed property regimes.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; nothing in queer anarchism bears on how regional language varieties are named.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists oppose state regulation and also the courts, but favour direct action by communities over lawsuits as the remedy.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from anti-hierarchy principles that a formal place for chiefs in lawmaking would be rejected.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that anarchists value freedom and would resist environmental rules imposed by the state.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The anthology favours prison and police abolition, which rules out fixed sentences imposed by the state.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and opposition to borders that adherents would reject state-imposed requirements on immigrants.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Anarchists oppose compulsory membership in any institution and favour voluntary association, though they back unions as workers' self-organisation; inferred from anti-statism.

voter-id.rationale: Queer anarchists reject state identification and border and citizenship regimes, and ID requirements would burden trans and undocumented people.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Rejecting the state means no religion holds legal precedence; inferred from anti-statism and anti-authoritarianism.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Anarchists reject the idea that elected rulers make a system democratic, preferring direct and horizontal self-government over electoral representation.

premarital-sex.rationale: Marriage is rejected as a state and patriarchal institution, and free love and relationship autonomy are central; Goldman's essay defends sex and love outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anarchists oppose state control of communications and repression of dissent, so shutdowns to maintain order are rejected.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Queer anarchists seek abolition of the state and of capitalism, not a state cash scheme, though they would prefer cash to punitive welfare bureaucracy; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal participation regardless of gender is basic to the movement, though anarchists reject office-holding in the state; the equal-rights part is affirmed.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Queer anarchists criticise organised religion as enforcing patriarchy and heteronormativity, but many are mixed on religion as a major cause; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Queer anarchism treats gender and sexual categories as socially constructed and critiques the biological fixity of identities; race is read the same way by its anti-hierarchy politics.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: State equality agencies are seen as part of the assimilationist state apparatus that queer anarchists reject in favour of autonomous community organising.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Anarchists reject property claims backed by the state, and queer anarchists link property to marriage and capitalism; a first-claim ownership theory is not discussed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Queer anarchists favour prison and police abolition and distrust state institutions, so they are inferred to reject state-run criminal courts; not directly discussed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Queer anarchists see religion as allied with the state and the gender binary, so literal scripture is inferred to be firmly rejected.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Queer anarchism demands that liberation include gender equality, but it would reject state-defined self-government; inferred at mild agreement.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Ending the state is central to queer anarchism, so a state of any economic kind would not be defended.

indirect-election.rationale: Anarchists favour direct and horizontal decision-making over hierarchies of delegates; not specifically discussed for offices.

national-church-status.rationale: Goldman's critique ties Church and State together and queer anarchists reject both, so a church with special legal status is firmly opposed.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Queer anarchists oppose the state and nationalism and favour autonomous communities, but territorial autonomy inside a state is not discussed.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; they reject nation-states, so deciding which state a territory joins is outside their frame.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Opposition to the state and its borders implies rejecting colonial borders as sacred; not directly discussed.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; they favour autonomous communities and anti-capitalism, but no source praises limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Anti-statism implies opposing state control of settlement even to protect Indigenous peoples; inferred, and solidarity with Indigenous peoples pulls the other way.

equal-conscription.rationale: Anarchists oppose conscription and militaries, so applying it to neither agrees with the statement; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Queer anarchism rejects nationalist and ancestral-land attachments as state ideology; inferred from its anti-statism and critique of belonging defined by borders.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Anarchists oppose state killing and punishment altogether, and the audit's police and prison abolition stance rules out summary executions; inferred from that.

close-ties-china.rationale: Queer anarchism has no stated view of China policy and rejects aligning with any state power; inferred, so left neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state and the idea of states championing their 'own' nationals abroad; inferred from anti-statism.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Anarchist traditions treat land and resources as held in common rather than owned, though compensation schemes are not discussed; inferred from that.

self-ownership.rationale: Queer anarchism stresses bodily autonomy and control over one's own relationships and body, though it rejects possessive-individualist property framing; inferred at low confidence.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Anarchists oppose regressive taxation but also taxation by the state in principle; a cut in consumption taxes is inferred as mildly favoured.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Queer anarchists favour mutual aid and universal access free of state gatekeeping over means-tested welfare; inferred from Conrad's criticism of benefits tied to status.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Anarchists distrust leaders and parties alike and want direct popular organisation rather than a leader-centred politics; the statement's premise of a leader is rejected.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Anarchists oppose state-granted privileges to business as an alliance of state and capital; inferred from the anti-state, anti-capitalist core.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Queer anarchism is anti-clerical and rejects religious authority over public and private life; inferred from its rejection of state-imposed norms.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The current rejects appeals to tradition and heteronormative ancestral values as authority; inferred from its critique of norms.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Goldman and later queer anarchists want relationships free of state and husband control, so a woman may end a marriage on her own; inferred from Marriage and Love.

national-resource-control.rationale: Anarchists oppose both national and corporate control of resources, favouring common or local control; inferred, with national control rejected as statist.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred: anti-capitalist anarchists see property holdings as the product of coercion and hierarchy, so the process does not legitimise unequal wealth.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: a state tax to tame finance is reformist, and the sources favour abolishing state and capitalism rather than regulating them.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Queer anarchism stresses intersecting oppressions, and Queering Anarchism treats racism as a continuing structure to be fought alongside gender and class.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred: anarchists deny that state law carries inherent authority, though they usually reject a natural-law framing of it.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from anti-work and anti-capitalist strands; the sources do not discuss automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: The sources do not address the geopolitical order; anarchists oppose all states and empires, not only a dominant one.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Anarchist currents are split, and the sources on queer anarchism do not discuss value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Anarchism rejects nationalism and the state, and the anti-assimilationist queer critique rejects national belonging as a norm.

material-over-identity.rationale: Queer anarchism holds that gender, sexuality and race oppression are not reducible to class and must be fought together with it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Anarchism rejects both parties' rule and the state, and the sources describe opposition to state and capitalism alike.

missingStatements.text: Marriage should not be a legal institution that confers state benefits and property rights.
missingStatements.rationale: Conrad argues marriage is tied to property transfers and state benefits and that health care should not depend on marital status.

missingStatements.text: Monogamy should not be treated as the default or ideal form of intimate relationship.
missingStatements.rationale: Relationship anarchy and polyamory are presented as anarchic, though Volcano warns against making nonmonogamy a new norm.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by traditional-family, where this audit answers negatively; relationship-form norms are not otherwise a separate axis.

missingStatements.text: Gay rights campaigns should not prioritise marriage, military service and hate crime laws.
missingStatements.rationale: The introduction describes an anti-assimilationist ethic rejecting these mainstream priorities.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to one movement's internal critique of gay-rights priorities; partly captured by abolish-legal-marriage and same-sex-marriage.

notes: Contributors disagree on polyamory as norm, on same-sex marriage rights versus the institution, and on armed militancy. Statements not covered by the sources are inferred from anti-statism and anti-capitalism.
